I farm only 2.0 mu, and my household is small, with some labor going off-farm, so I will keep my plan simple, steady, and practical. I already know wheat-maize well, and with 50 years of farming I would not take risks on such a small area. I will split the land across the usual rotation on the same 2.0 mu: wheat in the winter season, then maize in the summer season on the same field. Because I have well irrigation, I will rely on water at the key stages instead of gambling on rain. I will use improved seed for wheat and hybrid seed for maize because I want stable emergence, better yield, and less chance of losing output. I will use moderate fertilizer, not too little and not too much, because my land area is small and I want dependable returns rather than waste. I will use rotary tillage because it saves labor and fits a small farm like mine. I will spray only as needed but I still plan for basic weed, pest, and disease control so the crop can finish safely. My goal is stable grain yield with work I can manage myself.
